name: Public geosteering data beyond Kaggle: GWC 2020 semi-final typelog (DataverseNO), Alyaev & Elsheikh 2022 stratigraphy-realization generator (DataverseNO), GWC 2021 '10,000 interpretations and decisions' (Zenodo), Kaggle Geology Forecast Challenge 2025 (horizon traces), and open vertical/deviated log repositories usable as extra typelogs (FORCE 2020, Volve, KGS, UK NDR, NLOG, BC Energy Regulator)

code_availability: GWC 2020 typelog: gr.csv (230.6 KB) plus plotting script, CC BY 4.0. Stratigraphy realizations: data plus generator script on DataverseNO (license not checked) [uncertain]. GWC 2021: round1.zip (210 MB, unconventional) and round2.zip (51 MB, conventional) with JSON player data, interpolated interpretation CSVs, JSON schemas for player data and ground-truth 'answer', CC BY 4.0. Geology Forecast Challenge: data on Kaggle (train_raw CSVs with columns VS_APPROX_adjusted, HORIZON_Z_adjusted, geology_id), 1st-place notebooks BSD-2. FORCE 2020: NLOD 2.0. Volve: reported as CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (Databricks listing); earlier releases used an Equinor open-data licence [uncertain]. KGS, UK NDR, NLOG: free download; BCER: free FTP account via a request form.
evidence_level: Dataset landing pages, READMEs and JSON schemas read directly (GWC 2020, GWC 2021, Geology Forecast Challenge code). Alyaev & Elsheikh 2022 full text read (arXiv PDF): peer-reviewed. Repository descriptions for FORCE/Volve/KGS/NDR/NLOG/BCER from search snippets and official pages; whether GWC 2021 zips contain GR/typelog curves was NOT verified (not downloaded) [uncertain].
extreme_summary: Public geosteering data with the Kaggle task's exact structure (lateral GR + typewell GR + TVT truth) is almost nonexistent: the only open ROGII-style typelog is one synthetic Middle Woodford GR curve (GWC 2020), and the GWC 2021 release adds two ground-truth scenarios with ~10,000 expert interpretation snapshots. Beyond that, real typelogs must be taken from generic vertical-well repositories (FORCE 2020, UK NDR, KGS, NLOG), and real structural shapes from the Geology Forecast Challenge horizon traces, all of which need domain adaptation before they can feed our simulator.
task_definition: Not a method; a data-sourcing item. The goal is to find typelogs (GR vs TVT/TVD of an offset vertical well) and geometry (TVT/horizon vs MD/VS along laterals) outside the Kaggle set, to (a) diversify the 85% synthetic training wells, especially cases with repeated, self-similar layers, and (b) provide independent evaluation or calibration material. GWC 2020/2021 are ROGII StarSteer-style stratigraphy-based-steering tasks (match lateral GR to an offset typelog by adjusting the stratigraphic model); Geology Forecast Challenge asks for probabilistic forecasts of a layer-depth (horizon) curve ahead of the bit (10 realizations).
inputs: GWC 2020: one GR typelog (0.5 ft, normalized 0-1, synthetic, Middle Woodford, SCOOP Oklahoma). Alyaev 2022 realizations: randomly generated SVD (stratigraphic vertical depth) functions b*(x) with zero trend, used with that typelog to synthesize lateral GR via lookup. GWC 2021: well trajectories (md, tvd, vs, incl, azim), interpretation snapshots (md_points, horizon_depths, tvd_shifts, variable_thicknesses) every ~2 min per participant, ground-truth answer in the same format; log curves presumably embedded or referenced [uncertain]. Geology Forecast Challenge: horizon Z vs vertical section (VS) traces, one geology_id per source. FORCE 2020: 118 Norwegian North Sea wells, GR plus RHOB, NPHI, DTC, resistivities, lithology labels. Volve: ~24 wells incl. deviated/horizontal producers with GR, formation tops. KGS/NLOG/NDR/BCER: LAS files, GR present in most.
target_parameterisation: GWC/StarSteer answer files parameterise truth as horizon depths at MD points plus TVD shifts (a piecewise stratigraphic model); convertible to TVT along the trajectory, i.e. the same target as Kaggle TVT. Alyaev 2022 uses SVD(MD), which is exactly TVT up to sign/offset. Geology Forecast Challenge: HORIZON_Z_adjusted vs VS_APPROX_adjusted, i.e. a structural surface trace (equivalent to our z_layer = TVT + Z along the lateral). Vertical-well repositories provide only GR(TVD), i.e. typelog material, no TVT target.
output_representation: Not applicable (datasets). GWC 2021 is notable because it contains many human interpretations of the same well, an empirical distribution of plausible TVT paths per scenario; Geology Forecast Challenge scores 10 realizations per sample (probabilistic output).
architecture: Not applicable (datasets). Relevant generators: Alyaev 2022 builds training triples (reference typelog randomly trimmed to a short section, an SVD curve realization, and the synthetic lateral log) and trained a mixture density network on 28 million samples; the stratigraphy realization script is public. NORCE's interactive-geosteering-benchmark (github.com/geosteering-no/interactive-geosteering-benchmark, BSD-4) contains a multi-layer toy geomodel with an EM (resistivity) tool, not GR. Geology Forecast Challenge 1st place: Conv1D + multi-head attention with positional encoding, 5-fold, trained on 314,360 windows cut by the organisers' interpolation script.
core_mechanism: The value of external data here is distributional: our synthetic wells are generated only from the 773 Kaggle typewells (consolidated into ~60 master systems by seq_NN_master_typewell.py), so every synthetic repeated-layer pattern is one that already exists in Kaggle masters. New typelogs add new GR textures and new self-similarity structures; new horizon traces add new structural (dip/curvature) shapes for the z_shift / trend bank; GWC 2021 interpretations give human ambiguity statistics (spread of expert TVT paths) on known-truth wells.
training_objective: Not applicable (datasets). Geology Forecast Challenge metric is equivalent to a weighted MSE over forecast positions (per 1st-place writeup), with 10 realizations; Alyaev 2022 used a multiple-trajectory-prediction (winner-takes-all style) MDN loss.
evidence_scope: GWC 2020/2021: single lateral vs single typelog per scenario (2 scenarios in 2021). Geology Forecast Challenge: single horizon trace windows. Repositories: single vertical wells (multi-well fields in FORCE/Volve/NDR allow building typelog families from nearby wells).
prefix_conditioning: GWC 2021 snapshots are sequential (interpretation as drilling proceeds), so a prefix/suffix split can be emulated exactly like Kaggle's TVT_input; Geology Forecast Challenge windows are prefix-given forecasting (known part of the curve, predict the next 300 ft) [uncertain].
propose_vs_select: Not applicable (datasets). GWC 2021 human interpretations could serve as a candidate set for studying how often experts choose the wrong repeated band.
physical_constraints: Alyaev 2022 realizations assume layer-cake stratigraphy with constant thickness (log invariant along SVD), which is also Kaggle's implicit assumption; the 2021 GWC answer format has a 'variable_thicknesses' flag, so at least one scenario may break the constant-thickness assumption [uncertain].
dataset: (1) GWC 2020 semi-final typelog: 1 synthetic GR curve, 0.5 ft, normalized, Middle Woodford (SCOOP, Oklahoma); gr.csv 230.6 KB (roughly several thousand samples) [uncertain on exact length]. (2) Alyaev 2022 supporting data: stratigraphy realization curves + script; paper used 28M training / 12k validation / 10k test samples generated from these. (3) GWC 2021: 349 experts, ~10,000 snapshots, 2 scenarios (Round 1 unconventional, Round 2 conventional), 262 MB. (4) Geology Forecast Challenge: horizon traces from multiple geologies (geology_id), cut into windows (1st place obtained 314,360 samples); source basin not stated in what was read; organisers include ROGII so traces are plausibly from real StarSteer interpretations [uncertain]. (5) FORCE 2020: 118 wells, Norwegian North Sea, NLOD 2.0. (6) Volve: ~40,000 files, 24 wells incl. horizontal producers, Norwegian North Sea. (7) KGS: tens of thousands of LAS files, Kansas incl. Mississippian horizontal play [uncertain count]. (8) UK NDR: composite logs for ~12,000 offshore wellbores. (9) NLOG: thousands of Dutch wells, logs public after 5 years. (10) BCER: Montney and other BC wells, >90% of new Montney wells directional.
synthetic_to_real: GWC 2020 typelog is itself synthetic (built from Middle Woodford observations) and normalized to 0-1, so it must be quantile-mapped to Kaggle GR units (API) and noise-matched before use; Alyaev notes GWC used 6-7% log noise. Vertical-well repositories are real but from different basins and tools (North Sea clastics vs US unconventional carbonates/shales), so their GR textures and cycle thicknesses differ from Kaggle's; they need (a) GR normalization per well (quantiles), (b) resampling to 0.25 ft TVT levels, (c) optional thickness scaling to Kaggle cycle-length statistics. Our pipeline already has the machinery: master-typewell re-skinning (seq_NN_master_typewell.py) regenerates a simulated well's GR from a crop of another master, so external typelogs can enter as extra 'masters' in the re-skin bank.
metric_and_performance: No metric comparable to ours; datasets only. Reference points: Alyaev 2022 MDN on synthetic GWC-typelog data, best-mode errors well below the zero baseline (e.g. 7-mode predictor, test error 0.56 vs 0.94 baseline at 1% noise, units in their normalized SVD scale [uncertain]). GWC 2021 study: experts frequently missed the target (JPT 2022, 'geosteers often miss the target'); the robot of Muhammad et al. (SPE J 2025) was benchmarked on these scenarios. Geology Forecast Challenge: 1st place Conv1D+MHA ensemble (score not recorded here).
comparability: Not comparable to our pooled RMSE on 155 holdout wells; none of these sets has the Kaggle lateral+typewell+TVT label triple at scale. GWC 2021 could produce a tiny (2-well) out-of-distribution test with human baselines if the GR curves are in the zips [uncertain].
validation_protocol: For any use in training: external typelogs must be kept out of the internal 155-well holdout evaluation and results must be compared with a Kaggle-only control at the same epochs and seeds; because our acceptance noise is +-0.39 ft for a single run (and a seed-level null delta of -0.03 ft at 60 epochs), 2+ seeds or 5-fold CV are needed. For GWC 2021, the known-truth answer must not leak into any tuning if used as an external test.
inference_budget: No inference cost: data only affects training. Preprocessing (LAS parsing, normalization, resampling) is CPU minutes. GWC 2021 zips 262 MB; FORCE 2020 ~ hundreds of MB; Volve full set is large (tens of GB+) but only LAS logs are needed.
repeated_layers: This is the motivation, but the evidence is mixed. Real vertical logs from cyclic successions (e.g. North Sea Jurassic/Cretaceous, Kansas Pennsylvanian cyclothems) contain many self-similar GR cycles, which would create hard band-confusion cases the simulator does not currently produce from Kaggle masters alone. Caveat: our band confusion is defined relative to Kaggle typewells; if external logs are more (or differently) repetitive, the network may learn an ambiguity prior that is miscalibrated for Kaggle wells, which under the expectation decode directly raises RMSE (calibration, not accuracy, is what matters for pooled RMSE). A cheaper and in-distribution alternative is to mine Kaggle masters themselves for self-similar windows and upweight those in the simulator.
drift: Geology Forecast Challenge horizon traces are the relevant resource: they are real structural shapes along laterals (Z of a horizon vs VS), i.e. realistic dip/curvature histories, which could extend the real residual / trend bank used by z_shift (real_block residuals, TVT_bias_v2) and trajectory mixup; this targets the ~25% one-line-drift error mode by teaching the network more realistic slow dip changes. Typelogs do not help drift.
uncertainty_and_calibration: GWC 2021 gives, for the same well and same data, the spread of 349 expert interpretations over time, an empirical measure of how ambiguous each MD segment is; it could be used to check whether our posterior spread (width, number of humps) is larger where experts disagree. Geology Forecast Challenge is explicitly probabilistic (10 realizations). No calibration analyses exist in these releases.
where_to_use: (1) Synthetic generator: add external typelogs as extra master systems in the re-skin bank of experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_master_typewell.py (sim_cfg['reskin']), with low probability, after GR quantile normalization and 0.25 ft resampling. (2) Hard-case mining: compute a band-ambiguity score per typewell window (count and depth of secondary minima of the typewell self-cost |tw_gr(t) - tw_gr(t + s)| over the +-50 ft level window) and oversample high-ambiguity crops, from Kaggle masters first, external logs second. (3) Drift augmentation: add Geology Forecast Challenge horizon traces (converted to z_layer increments per MD) to the z_shift real-residual bank. (4) External sanity test: convert GWC 2021 scenarios (if GR is included) into Kaggle format and score the model plus compare with the human-expert spread; tiny N, qualitative only.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%) via harder / more diverse repeated-layer synthetic cases; drift (~25%) via real structural traces (Geology Forecast Challenge); calibration of hump weights secondarily.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Today all synthetic wells are generated from Kaggle's own 773 typewells / ~60 master systems and Kaggle trajectories (Ruby's simulator + diff-block bootstrap, trajectory mixup, real_block residuals, re-skinning between Kaggle masters). No external typelog, horizon trace, or expert-interpretation data is used anywhere, and there is no explicit hard-case (self-similarity) sampling: synthetic crops are drawn without regard to how ambiguous the typewell window is. The closest experiment, rb_v2_synth (mixup + re-skin + real residuals, bundled), was worse than baseline at 60 epochs (+0.362 ft) and still +0.147 at 150 epochs but still descending and better on the bulk of wells (median 2.796 vs 2.929), with losses on a few catastrophic wells; the three sub-changes were never ablated. So the 'more diverse typelogs' direction is unresolved rather than refuted, and adding out-of-basin typelogs is a stronger version of the same intervention, with larger distribution shift.
proposed_experiment: E0 (CPU, no training, half a day): download the GWC 2020 gr.csv plus ~50-100 GR logs from FORCE 2020 (NLOD) and KGS; normalize each by quantiles to the Kaggle typewell GR distribution, resample to 0.25 ft. Define an ambiguity index per 100 ft window: number of secondary minima within 20% of the primary minimum of the windowed self-matching cost over shifts 5-50 ft. Compare the index distribution of Kaggle masters vs external logs and, crucially, correlate the index of each holdout well's typewell window with its per-well SSE and wrong_mode share from the existing posterior dump (results/baseline_check_posterior_all). Go/no-go: proceed only if high-ambiguity typewell windows explain a large share of wrong_mode error AND Kaggle's own masters contain few such windows (i.e. there is a coverage gap external data could fill). E1 (in-distribution control first): in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_master_typewell.py add ambiguity-weighted crop sampling from Kaggle masters only (new sim_cfg key, e.g. 'hard_crop_weight_power'); 150 epochs, 2 seeds, vs baseline 150 epochs 2 seeds, MD-phase TTA on both. E2: add external typelogs as extra masters in the re-skin bank (new sim_cfg['reskin']['external_masters'] path list, apply_prob 0.1-0.2, so external logs are <=10% of synthetic wells); same protocol; success = pooled RMSE gain beyond run-to-run scatter across both seeds, with the tail wells (fb03ae90, f6d009f4, f2d4c8c9, e7818f7a, d7eb0be8) inspected. E3 (drift): convert Geology Forecast Challenge traces into per-MD z_layer increment series, append to the real_block residual bank with a mixing probability, 150 epochs 2 seeds. E4 (optional): if GWC 2021 zips include the lateral and typelog GR, build two Kaggle-format wells and compare model posterior spread with the expert-interpretation spread per MD.
implementation_effort: E0 low (LAS parsing with lasio, numpy). E1 low-medium (sampling weights inside the existing simulator). E2 medium (external master ingestion, GR normalization, making re-skin quantile placement work for masters without Kaggle drilling bands). E3 medium (coordinate conversion of VS/Z traces). E4 medium, blocked on verifying zip contents.
gpu_cost: E0 CPU only. E1-E3: each is a pair of 150-epoch ConvNeXt-small trainings per seed (roughly 5 h per run on the RTX 5060 8 GB at the documented ~110-120 s/epoch), so 2 seeds x (candidate + control) ~ 20 h per hypothesis; control runs can be shared across E1-E3.
distillation_compatibility: Fully compatible: data changes only affect the teacher's training (and optionally the student's KD data); the FastViT student distilled on output posteriors inherits any gain without architectural change.
error_correlation_with_ours: Low diversity: same architecture and decode, so errors stay correlated; the benefit, if any, is a better-calibrated single model rather than a new blend member. Models trained with and without external masters could be averaged as a mild ensemble, similar to the existing ConvNeXt ensemble.
risk: (1) Distribution shift: external typelogs are from other basins/tools; the net may learn textures or ambiguity priors that do not transfer, and under the expectation decode a miscalibrated ambiguity prior raises RMSE. (2) The only exact-format open typelog (GWC 2020) is a single synthetic curve, possibly near-duplicate of a Kaggle typewell (same organiser ROGII) [uncertain]; it adds little diversity. (3) Prior evidence: bundled synthetic diversification (rb_v2_synth) has not beaten baseline on this holdout; the holdout is decided by ~10 catastrophic wells, so a real but small gain may be unmeasurable without seeds/folds. (4) Licensing: Volve is non-commercial (CC BY-NC-SA) [uncertain]; KGS/NDR/NLOG terms need checking before redistribution; BCER needs an account. (5) Effort vs payoff: the bottleneck may be evidence in the input (band identity is ambiguous given the data) rather than training-set diversity; harder synthetic cases then teach the net to spread mass more, which lowers RMSE only if the added spread matches true ambiguity. (6) GWC 2021 content uncertain until the zips are inspected.
notes: Downloads were not performed in this research pass (per session rules); zip contents of GWC 2021 remain unverified. Alyaev & Elsheikh 2022 is also covered under A09 (multi-hypothesis MDN); their public stratigraphy-realization script is a simple, documented synthetic-curve generator that could be compared with Ruby's simulator. Geology Forecast Challenge is a ROGII/NORCE-organised sibling competition (2025) of the ROGII Kaggle competition and is the only other public dataset with real lateral-scale structural traces; it was co-authored by I. Kuvaev (ROGII), linking it to the Kaggle data source. CREStereo (see B01) is the stereo-matching precedent for this item: its authors attribute robustness on repetitive-texture regions largely to a synthetic dataset designed around hard cases, which supports hard-case mining (E1) over indiscriminate diversification. Overlaps: A01/A02 (GWC studies), A09 (Alyaev MDN), B11 (synthetic data and sim-to-real).
